rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a long vowel precedes pronominal hāʾ, dropping its following yāʾ or wāw in connected speech is preferred; Sībawayh favors these shortened readings but accepts full realization as Arabic.
rows.anchor: فلما اجتمعت حروف متشابهة حذفوا وهو أحسن وأكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Separate accusative pronouns use the form إيا when a corresponding attached suffix is unavailable; where a suffix can attach, speakers use it instead.
rows.anchor: لأنهم استغنوا بها عن إيا كما استغنوا بالتاء وأخواتها في الرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أيّ, whether annexed or independent, behaves like من; the verse’s independent أيا ما تدعو is good Arabic, just as the annexed construction is.
rows.anchor: قال الله عز وجل ^ ( أيا ما تدعو فله الأسماء الحسنى ) ^ فحسن كحسنه مضافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In أيها تشاء لك, تشاء completes أي as a relative clause like الذي; the conditional version may use a jussive, with the construction changing when فاء is supplied. من behaves similarly.
rows.anchor: فتشاء صلة لأيها حتى كمل اسما ثم بنيت لك على أيها

rows.speaker: ناس وهم الكوفيون
rows.claim: Harun reports that Kufans read أيهم in 19:69 with the nominative form; Sībawayh calls this a good dialect and says they treat أي like a relative pronoun, as in their phrase امرر على أيهم أفضل.
rows.anchor: وحدثنا هارون أن ناسا وهم الكوفيون يقرءونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khalil explains the raised أيهم in اضرب أيهم أفضل as quoted speech, as if one says ‘strike the one called which of them is best’; Sībawayh judges this account remote, allowing it only in poetry or necessity.
rows.anchor: وتفسير الخليل رحمه الله ذلك

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus treats the construction like أشهد إنك لرسول الله and suspends the verb; Sībawayh says this account does not resemble that example.
rows.anchor: وأما يونس فيزعم أنه بمنزلة قولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regular analogy makes أي accusative, like اضرب الذين أفضل; Sībawayh accepts this ordinary parsing while preserving attested Arabic forms.
rows.anchor: وأما الذين نصبوا فقاسوه وقالوا هو بمنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh cautions against extending an anomalous, weakly attested construction by analogy; if Arabs use it, it must be followed as reported.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبغي لك أن تقيس على الشاذ المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If bare أي were treated as a definite relative pronoun like its annexed form, Sībawayh says it would take no tanwīn when definite and would take tanwīn when indefinite.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة الذي معرفة أن لا ينون

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhtal’s line is cited by al-Khalil as poetic evidence for the quoted-speech analysis of the construction.
rows.anchor: بقول الأخطل # % ولقد أبيت من الفتاة بمنزل %

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أبي وأيك كان شرا means which of me and you was worse: the two do not share one أي, but each person is considered separately.
rows.anchor: ولكنه أخلصه لكل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh cites al-Abbas ibn Mirdas’s line فأيى ما وأيك كان شرا as evidence for the paired أي construction asking which of two was worse.
rows.anchor: فأيى ما وأيك كان شرا

rows.speaker: خداش بن زهير
rows.claim: Khidash ibn Zuhayr’s line أيي وأيكم أعز وأمنع attests the paired construction meaning which one of me and you is stronger and more protected.
rows.anchor: وقال خداش بن زهير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh cites Khidash ibn Zuhayr’s second line فأيي وأى ابن الحصين as another attestation of the same distributive أي construction.
rows.anchor: غداة التقينا كان عندك أعذرا

words: أي الحزبين أحصى لما لبثوا أمدا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أيها أزكى طعاما is an interrogative nominal clause inside the larger object of فلينظر; its question structure cannot be governed internally by a preceding verb because the interrogative hamza blocks it. Sībawayh compares the question in 18:12.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى @QB@ فلينظر أيها أزكى طعاما @QE@

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām of initiation likewise prevents علمت from governing what follows; Sībawayh says it enters for emphasis and certainty, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: فهذه اللام تمنع العمل كما تمنع ألف الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh parses ورسوله as a fresh nominal start after إن الله بريء من المشركين, paralleling an emphasized nominal sentence such as إن زيدا منطلق.
rows.anchor: ^ ( أن الله برئ من المشركين ورسوله ) ^

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without an interrogative or lām of initiation, علمت works transitively like عرفت and رأيت; Sībawayh supports this with the cited verses.
rows.anchor: لأعملت علمت كما تعمل عرفت ورأيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the question itself begins the complement, as in قد عرفت أبو من زيد, it must be nominative; the accusative أبو من construction is possible when first framed as a separate question and then governed by the verb.
rows.anchor: قد عرفت أبو من زيد لم يجز إلا الرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With أرأيتك, the first object must be accusative because the verb means ‘tell me about Zayd’ and requires a second object, which the interrogative clause supplies.
rows.anchor: لا يحسن فيه إلا النصب فى زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أي يوم in قد عرفت أي يوم الجمعة is accusative when it functions as an adverbial ظرف; if it is not adverbial, it is nominative. Arabs also vary in the case of أي حين عقبتي.
rows.anchor: وإن لم تجعله ظرفا رفعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the poetic phrase والدهر أيتما حال دهارير, أيتما حال is adverbial and means in every state or every time.
rows.anchor: فإنما هو بمنزلة قولك والدهر دهارير كل حال وكل مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh requires هو after the subject in this embedded question: an interrogative cannot rely on preceding material and instead needs what follows it.
rows.anchor: لا يستغنى بما قبله إنما يستغنى بما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وَ coordinates two items without assigning precedence to the first; مررت بزيد وعمرو can leave open which was first or describe one simultaneous passage, and the negative does not establish an order.
rows.anchor: فالواو أشركت بينهما فى الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فَ coordinates the two events while making the first the starting point, as in passing Zayd and then Amr.
rows.anchor: فالفاء شركت بينهما فى المرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثُمَّ marks two passages and makes the first one the starting point while coordinating both under the preposition.
rows.anchor: فالمرور ههنا مروران وجعلت ثم الأول مبدوءا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أَوْ coordinates alternatives, asserting passage for one rather than both; a denial of both is phrased ما مررت بواحد منهما, while denying one names that one.
rows.anchor: وأثبتت المرور لأحدهما دون الآخر وسوت بينهما فى الدعوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لَا coordinates the two nouns while affirming the passage of the first and excluding the second, clarifying which one was meant.
rows.anchor: عند من التبسا عليه فلم يدر بأيهما مررت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medially weak verbs form verbal nouns and active participles in varied ways: بعته بيعا and كلته كيلا yield بائع and كائل, like strong-root ضربه ضربا وهو ضارب.
rows.anchor: تقول بعته بيعا وكلته كيلا فأنا أكيله وأبيعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For زار، عاد, and حاك, speakers use زيارة، عيادة, and حياكة, as if avoiding the expected فعول pattern because of its wāw and ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقالوا زرته زيارة وعدته عيادة وحكته حياكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خافه takes خوفا and خائف by analogy with لقمه لقما, because the verbs match in form and transitivity; some Arabs also say خاف for a man by analogy with فرق and فزع.
rows.anchor: جعلوه بمنزلة لقمته فأنا ألقمه لقما وهو لاقم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other patterns include نلته نيلا, ذمته ذاما, and عبته عابا or عيبا; Sībawayh compares them with regular transitive forms such as جرعه جرعا and حمده حمدا.
rows.anchor: كما قالوا جرعه جرعا وهو جارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms سؤته سوءا and وقته قوتا follow فعلا, like شغلته شغلا; عفته عيافة is another alternative to a فعول verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقالوا سؤته سوءا وقته قوتا وساءني سوءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some hollow verbs form verbal nouns on فعول, such as سرت سؤورا and غرت غؤورا, alongside the strong-root patterns جمود، قعود، سقوط; الغؤور والغيار describe entering into something.
rows.anchor: وقالوا غرت فأنا أغور غؤورا وهو غائر

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhtal’s line سارت إليهم سؤور attests the hollow-verb verbal noun سؤور.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخطل # % لما أتوها بمصباح

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s line سرت إليه في أعالي السور is cited as poetic evidence for the form of this hollow verb.
rows.anchor: وقال العجاج # % ورب ذي سرداق محجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh gives غابت الشمس غيوبا and بادت تبيد بيودا; the latter is the verse’s verb, and both follow patterns like strong-root جلس جلوسا and نفر نفورا.
rows.anchor: كما قالوا جلس يجلس جلوسا ونفر ينفر نفورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قَام and صام use قياما and صياما to avoid فعول; آبت الشمس takes إيابا, with أؤوبا also reported, compared with غؤور، سؤور, and the strong-root رجوع.
rows.anchor: وقالوا آبت الشمس إيابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other verbs avoid فعول with patterns such as نياحة، عيافة، قيافة and صيَاح، غياب; Sībawayh says this avoidance appears with yāʾ roots as it does with wāw roots.
rows.anchor: وقالوا صاح صياحا وغابت الشمس غيابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دام، زال, and راح use دواما، زوالا, and رواحا rather than فعول; similar patterns include حاضت حيضا، صامت صوما، حالت حولا, and مالت ميلا, supported by strong-root analogues.
rows.anchor: وله نظائر أيضا الذهاب والثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb لعت has لعت and لاعا patterns, while دئت yields داء; some also say لائع by analogy with بائع, though لاع is more common.
rows.anchor: وقالوا لعت تلاع لاعا وهو لاع
